description: issue #847 regression: `clear_screen`'s homing MUST be observable in the trace stream, so a consumer that replays events agrees with the runtime instead of silently disagreeing with it. This is the exact reproduction from the issue: with a single turtle and no optional profiles, `forward 10` / `right 45` / `clear_screen` used to emit only `clear{mode:"clear_screen"}`, leaving a replaying consumer at [0 10] heading 45 while the `print pos` / `print heading` that follow report [0 0] and 0. Now the homing emits `move` ([0 10] -> [0 0], reporting the pre-reset heading 45 exactly as `home` does) then `turn` (45 -> 0) before the `clear`, so a fold of the events and the runtime's own state agree on both position and heading. spec/rendering.md:151 makes the `clear` PAYLOAD the minimum mechanism ("MUST distinguish drawing-only clearing from clear-and-home behavior so playback and debugging can reproduce state exactly"); the homing pair is a deliberate, permitted superset of that minimum, sparing every consumer a `clear_screen`-shaped special case since animation, stepping, `why`, and `debug` already track position and heading through `move`/`turn` for every other turtle command. The pen is DOWN throughout (the program never lifts it) and yet NO `draw-segment` accompanies the homing `move`: the same instruction subsequently clears the drawing, so a line back to the origin would be exactly the artifact the clear removes - spec/rendering.md:36's "a pen-down move appends one straight segment" describes what a move contributes to the RETAINED SCENE, and spec/rendering.md:148's "Clear operations" row fixes `clear_screen`'s contribution at *cleared*. The spec does not settle this explicitly; the reading is escalated to the maintainer as issue #858. `move` and `draw-segment` are independent event kinds, so "moved but drew nothing" needs no renderer-side special case - contrast the `forward 10` at seq 1/2, where the same pen state DOES produce a `draw-segment`.
